# Shell fact counters (Bash, POSIX sh, ksh93): one per line, label TAB pattern (Java regex), counted
# over the whole file. The [ignore] line runs first and reads the file as the shell does, leftmost
# region first: it blanks comments (a whole line, or from a # after a blank to the end of the line)
# and heredoc bodies, keeping the line breaks, so a function or a "set -e" quoted for a remote shell
# does not count as this script's, and a heredoc marker inside a comment opens nothing. A heredoc may
# end at any word, quoted or not (<<EOF, <<'END-OF-SQL', <<!); its end marker stands alone on its
# line, after tabs only for <<-; a heredoc whose marker never comes runs to the end of the file, as
# bash reads it. A << inside (( )), $(( )) or $[ ] is a shift (read up to 120 characters back, or
# over up to three groups in parentheses, each with up to two of its own), and one whose line goes on with an
# unclosed quote sits inside a string (the rest of that line is blanked); neither opens a heredoc,
# so a long file of either stays
# linear. A function body may be any compound command ({, (, if, for, while, until, case, select,
# [[). "exported variables" and "readonly variables" count every name of a line
# (export A=1 B=2 is two), not functions (export -f); "script-level assignments" leaves out the
# environment prefix of a command (LC_ALL=C sort). Counts are regex heuristics: a function defined
# inside a string, an option arm written on one line with others, the second of two heredocs started
# on one line, a blank and # inside a quoted string (read as a comment), and a value with more than
# one level of $( ) are not read as the shell reads them. ShellFactPatternsTest pins every case;
# ProfileFactPatternsLinearityTest measures that every pattern of the profile reads linearly.
[ignore] comments and heredoc bodies
functions
getopts loops
getopts option letters
dash-option case arms
named positional parameters
exported variables
readonly variables
defaulted variables
script-level assignments
sourced files
traps
set -e
exit statements with a status
typeset and declare declarations
ksh discipline functions
